scope: Only the fresh-reader SHM-open-denial and CANTINIT fallback source branch; not full WAL design or runtime admission
required_preconditions: A fresh independent reader process, so no pShm or per-inode pShmNode from an already-open connection is reused.
Fixed unix-posix VFS and ordinary WAL mode; no preselected heap/no-SHM/exclusive path.
The query requires the WAL-only committed sentinel; denial reaches the engine rather than an earlier metadata guard.
The SHM read-denial policy actually denies the fixed SHM path.

source_chain.finding: A process-local existing pShmNode can be reused; the fresh-reader condition is material.
readonly_shm=1 skips the SHM O_RDWR|O_CREAT open. Failure of the subsequent O_RDONLY|O_NOFOLLOW open sets SQLITE_CANTOPEN_BKPT and branches to shm_open_err.
The error label purges/free resources and returns the same rc.
unixShmMap returns any non-OK unixOpenSharedMemory result immediately.
Ordinary WAL calls sqlite3OsShmMap. Only READONLY-family codes get the readOnly flag, and only plain SQLITE_READONLY becomes OK; CANTOPEN is returned unchanged.
Only SQLITE_READONLY_CANTINIT selects the unreliable-SHM heap path here. All other non-OK results, including this CANTOPEN, return as errors.

limitations: W03 is a dependency-negative control, not proof that readonly_shm was recognized: default O_RDWR denial followed by O_RDONLY denial can also fail.
Actual installed sqlite_source_id, the fixed available VFS and positive W01 remain independent gates.
A writable-open attempt is still possible for the WAL: wal.c1725 uses READWRITE|CREATE and os_unix.c6684-6702 may downgrade after denial. This review does not claim zero write attempts.
No host calls, private input access, SQLite execution, synthetic case execution, new retry or deadline change occurred.
No broader statement is made about every WAL fallback or engine error path.
